concepts.title: Glycolysis and Its Net ATP Gain
concepts.definition: Glycolysis is the partial oxidation of one glucose molecule to two molecules of pyruvic acid through ten enzymatic steps in the cytoplasm, producing a net gain of two ATP and two NADH under anaerobic conditions.
concepts.key_idea: Glycolysis splits hexose into two triose sugars through a prepatory phase using ATP and a payoff phase generating ATP and NADH, and it is common to aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

concepts.title: Fermentation: Anaerobic Fate of Pyruvate
concepts.definition: Under anaerobic conditions pyruvic acid is reduced by NADH to lactic acid in muscles or to ethanol and carbon dioxide in yeast, and fermentation yields only a net gain of two ATP per glucose with far less energy released than aerobic respiration.
concepts.key_idea: The enzymes pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase carry out alcoholic fermentation in yeast, and lactic acid fermentation happens in muscle cells during exercise.

concepts.title: Aerobic Respiration: Link Reaction, Krebs Cycle and ETS Net ATP
concepts.definition: Aerobic respiration oxidises pyruvate through the link reaction forming acetyl CoA, the Krebs cycle in the mitochondrial matrix, and the electron transport system on the inner membrane with oxidative phosphorylation, giving a net gain of thirty-eight ATP molecules from one glucose molecule.
concepts.key_idea: The complete oxidation of one glucose through glycolysis, link reaction, Krebs cycle and ETS accounts for thirty-eight ATP, with most ATP arising from NADH and FADH2 oxidation in oxidative phosphorylation.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the number of glucose molecules oxidised by 38 to get the net ATP of aerobic respiration

concepts.title: Respiratory Quotient of Substrates
concepts.definition: The respiratory quotient is the ratio of the volume of carbon dioxide released to the volume of oxygen consumed in respiration, and it equals one for carbohydrates, is less than one for fats and proteins, and can exceed one for organic acids.
concepts.key_idea: The RQ of germinating fats like castor seeds is less than one because fat oxidation consumes more oxygen than the carbon dioxide it releases, while succulents show RQ of zero in daylight.

solution_steps.explain: Divide the volume of carbon dioxide released by the volume of oxygen consumed to get the respiratory quotient

concepts.title: Amphibolic Pathway and Respiratory Balance Sheet
concepts.section: 12.4.4 The Respiratory Balance Sheet, 12.4.5 Amphibolic Pathway
concepts.definition: Respiration is an amphibolic pathway because the respiratory intermediates serve both catabolism and anabolism, and the respiratory balance sheet is theoretical since ATP amounts depend on the shuttle of electrons, the mitochondrial state and the pathway taken.
concepts.key_idea: Acetyl CoA drawn from fats, carbohydrates and proteins enters the same Krebs cycle, proving the amphibolic nature of respiration.
